name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
addr: 14200 US-1, Juno Beach, FL 33408
kid: A real sea turtle hospital! Meet turtles getting better, see their x-rays, and find out when the next one goes back to the ocean.
dad: Pick one patient together and follow its story on the center's board. Fish feeding is Tuesdays and Thursdays.
tip: Free (donation box). Open daily. Pair it with the pier next door.
wonder: Why do mother turtles come back to the exact beach where they hatched?

name: Juno Beach Pier
addr: 14775 US-1, Juno Beach, FL 33408
kid: Walk way out over the ocean, spot rays and fish under the water, and maybe catch one yourself. Sunrise here is unreal.
dad: Rent rods at the bait shop and teach them to bait a hook. Go for sunrise once; it will be a core memory.
tip: Small walk-on fee, rod rentals at the shop. Early morning is calmest.
wonder: Why does the water change color as you walk farther out on the pier?

name: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse
addr: 500 Captain Armour's Way, Jupiter, FL 33469
kid: Climb 105 steps inside a giant red lighthouse from 1860 and look out over the whole inlet. You have to be 48 inches tall to climb!
dad: Measure them at home first (48 in). Count steps out loud together, then find your car from the top.
tip: Closed-toe shoes required. Kids under 16 climb with an adult. Check climb times before you go.
wonder: How did ships find the inlet at night before the lighthouse was built in 1860?

name: Busch Wildlife Sanctuary
addr: 17855 Rocky Pines Rd, Jupiter, FL 33478
kid: Florida panthers, black bears, bald eagles, alligators and owls, all rescued and living on shady trails you walk through.
dad: Let them pick the trail order. Ask a keeper which animal arrived most recently.
tip: Donation-based entry. Open daily 10–4:30. Shaded, stroller-friendly paths.
wonder: Why can't a rescued panther just go back to the wild once it's healed?

name: DuBois Park Lagoon
addr: 19075 DuBois Rd, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: A calm, clear lagoon right by the lighthouse where you can snorkel with tiny fish, build sand forts and watch boats go by.
dad: First snorkel lesson: shallow water, no waves. Bring a bucket and a fish ID card.
tip: Free parking. Go on an incoming tide for the clearest water. Grills and picnic tables.
wonder: Why are the little fish in the lagoon not afraid of us?

name: Rapids Water Park
addr: 6566 N Military Trail, Riviera Beach, FL 33407
kid: Forty-two slides, a lazy river and a huge wave pool. Splish Splash Lagoon has slides just your size, and Big Thunder is seven stories tall.
dad: Ride everything they dare you to. Lazy river at the end is where the talking happens.
tip: Open mid-March through Labor Day, weekends in fall. Arrive at opening to beat lines.
wonder: How does a slide make you go fast without any motor?

name: Palm Beach Zoo
addr: 1301 Summit Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
kid: Jaguars, koalas, otters, a carousel and a splash fountain for when it gets hot. Small enough to see everything in one visit.
dad: Give each kid a 'find it' list of five animals. Winner picks the snack.
tip: Go early; animals are most active before 11. Splash pad means pack a towel.
wonder: Why do koalas sleep almost all day?

name: Cox Science Center & Aquarium
addr: 4801 Dreher Trail N, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
kid: Touch tanks, a planetarium, baby alligators, dinosaur fossils and a mini golf course outside. Press every button.
dad: Best rainy-day plan in the county. Do a planetarium show together and talk about what you saw on the drive home.
tip: Indoor, air conditioned. Planetarium shows are extra. Right next to the zoo.
wonder: What do you think it feels like on Mars? Ask the planetarium host.

name: Lion Country Safari
addr: 2003 Lion Country Safari Rd, Loxahatchee, FL 33470
kid: Drive your own car through a safari with rhinos, giraffes and zebras walking right past your window. Then rides, a splash park and giraffe feeding.
dad: Let them be the spotters and narrate from the back seat. Feed a giraffe together.
tip: Windows up in the lion area. Half the day is the drive-through, half is the walk-through park.
wonder: Why do giraffes have such long tongues?

name: Manatee Lagoon
addr: 6000 N Flagler Dr, West Palm Beach, FL 33407
kid: On cold winter days, dozens of manatees float right under the deck to stay warm. Count how many noses pop up!
dad: Check the manatee cam the morning of a cold snap and go when the count is high.
tip: Free. Manatee season is Nov 15 to Mar 31; closed Mondays the rest of the year.
wonder: Why do manatees come to this exact spot when it gets cold?

name: Peanut Island by Boat
addr: Riviera Beach Marina, 200 E 13th St, Riviera Beach, FL 33404
kid: Take a shuttle boat to a tiny island with a snorkel lagoon full of parrotfish, a walking trail all the way around, and a real Cold War bunker.
dad: Pack a picnic; there are no stores on the island. Snorkel the lagoon together, then walk the loop.
tip: Shuttle boat from the marina or water taxi from Sailfish Marina. Weekdays are far quieter.
wonder: Why was a secret bunker built on a tiny island for a president?

name: Riverbend Park Bikes & Kayaks
addr: 9060 W Indiantown Rd, Jupiter, FL 33478
kid: Ten miles of shady bike trails with deer, turtles and peacocks, plus kayaks you can paddle down a real river.
dad: Rent bikes or kayaks on site. Let them lead the ride and choose where to stop for snacks.
tip: Free park entry; rentals from Jupiter Outdoor Center inside the park. Bring bug spray.
wonder: How can a river flow in two directions depending on the tide?

name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park
addr: 16450 SE Federal Hwy, Hobe Sound, FL 33455
kid: Climb Hobe Mountain tower (the tallest 'mountain' around!), ride a boat up the river to a pioneer's camp, and look for gators.
dad: Do the Loxahatchee Queen boat tour to Trapper Nelson's camp. Camp here one night when they're ready.
tip: Park entry is per car. Boat tour runs on set days; book ahead.
wonder: Why is the 'mountain' here only 86 feet tall, and why is that the tallest around?

name: Blowing Rocks Preserve
addr: 574 S Beach Rd, Hobe Sound, FL 33455
kid: Waves crash into holes in the rocks and shoot up like geysers, sometimes 50 feet high! Then explore tide pools.
dad: Check the tide chart: high tide with east wind makes the big blows. Tide pools at low tide are the quiet version.
tip: Small donation entry. Water shoes. Small lot fills early on weekends.
wonder: What makes the water shoot up through the rocks like a geyser?

name: Baseball at Roger Dean Stadium
addr: 4751 Main St, Jupiter, FL 33458
kid: Cheer for the Jupiter Hammerheads, chase foul balls, and eat a hot dog under the lights. Some nights end with fireworks.
dad: Teach them to keep score for a few innings. Sit on the grass berm the first time.
tip: Minor league season runs April to September; spring training in February and March.
wonder: How does a pitcher make a ball curve in the air?

name: Downtown Palm Beach Gardens
addr: 11701 Lake Victoria Gardens Ave, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
kid: Ride the carousel, run through the dancing fountains, and get ice cream. Five minutes from home!
dad: The easy weeknight win. Carousel, fountain, ice cream, done before bedtime.
tip: Carousel rides are a few dollars. Check the events calendar for movie and music nights.
wonder: How do the fountains know when to jump?

name: Lighthouse Cove Adventure Golf
addr: 617 N Hwy A1A, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: Thirty-six holes of mini golf with waterfalls, caves and a pirate ship, then a burger and ice cream at the shack.
dad: Play one course each, loser buys ice cream. Perfect after a Carlin Park beach morning.
tip: Across from the beach on A1A. Evenings are cooler and the course lights up.
wonder: Why does a golf ball roll farther on short grass than on carpet?

name: MacArthur Beach State Park
addr: 10900 Jack Nicklaus Dr, North Palm Beach, FL 33408
kid: Cross a long boardwalk over the lagoon to a wild beach, kayak the estuary, and visit the nature center with its fish tanks.
dad: Rent a tandem kayak and let them steer. The boardwalk walk is where they'll tell you about school.
tip: Per-car entry. Kayak rentals at the nature center. Quiet beach with no buildings in sight.
wonder: Why are mangrove roots sticking up out of the water?

name: Grassy Waters Preserve
addr: 8264 Northlake Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33412
kid: A boardwalk through a real Everglades swamp with gators, herons and turtles. Bring binoculars and whisper.
dad: Make a sightings tally on a card. Ask about the guided canoe trips for when they're ready.
tip: Free. Mornings are coolest and the wildlife is out. Closed some weekdays; check.
wonder: Where does the water in our kitchen tap actually come from?

name: Loxahatchee River Center
addr: 805 N US-1, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: Touch tanks with sea stars and crabs, big aquariums, and the story of how the river flows from the swamp to the ocean.
dad: A small, quiet place where they can ask a staffer a hundred questions. Combine with a picnic at Burt Reynolds Park.
tip: Free. In Burt Reynolds Park. Check hours; closed Sundays and Mondays.
wonder: How does rain in the Everglades end up in the ocean at Jupiter?

name: Altitude Trampoline Park
addr: 4340 Okeechobee Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33409
kid: Wall-to-wall trampolines, dodgeball, a foam pit, ninja course and basketball dunk lanes. Jump until you can't.
dad: Buy a jump pass for yourself too. Dodgeball against dad is the whole point.
tip: Grip socks required (buy there). Book a time slot online on weekends.
wonder: Why do you bounce higher when you jump with someone else?

name: Ice Skating at Palm Beach Ice Works
addr: 1590 N Florida Mango Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33409
kid: Real ice in Florida! Public skate sessions with rental skates and a snack bar. Hold the wall, then let go.
dad: Hold hands for the first lap and then let them go. Hot chocolate after.
tip: Public skate times vary; check the schedule. Bring gloves and long pants.
wonder: Why is ice slippery?

name: Carlin Park Beach Day
addr: 400 S State Rd A1A, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: A big lifeguarded beach with gentle waves for boogie boards, plus a playground and a snack bar. Try a surf lesson one day!
dad: Boogie boards first, then book a kids' surf lesson from one of the Jupiter surf schools for a milestone day.
tip: Free parking. Lifeguards on duty. Lighthouse Cove mini golf is across the street.
wonder: Where do waves come from on a day with no wind?

name: Sunset Celebration at Sailfish Marina
addr: 98 Lake Dr, Palm Beach Shores, FL 33404
kid: Thursday night sunset party on the docks: artists, music, and giant fish and pelicans right under the pier waiting for scraps.
dad: Buy a bag of fish food, stand at the end of the dock and watch the sun go down together.
tip: Thursday evenings. Free to walk around. The water taxi to Peanut Island leaves from here too.
wonder: Why do pelicans dive like that and not hurt themselves?

name: Norton Museum of Art
addr: 1450 S Dixie Hwy, West Palm Beach, FL 33401
kid: A huge art museum with a giant banyan tree, a sculpture garden, and family art-making days where you make your own.
dad: Pick one painting each and tell its story to each other. Look up the free family days before you go.
tip: Check the calendar for free days and family programs. Great on a hot or rainy afternoon.
wonder: What do you think the artist was feeling when they painted this?

name: Horseback Riding in Jupiter Farms
addr: Desert Rose Ranch, Ranch Colony, Jupiter, FL 33478
kid: Brush a horse, learn to hold the reins, and ride around a real ranch. Every horse has a name and a personality.
dad: Book a beginner lesson for both of you. Learning something new side by side is the point.
tip: Call ahead; small stables book up. Long pants and closed shoes. Several Jupiter Farms ranches offer kids' lessons.
wonder: How does a horse know what you want from the reins?

name: Sea Turtle Release on the Beach
addr: Loggerhead Marinelife Center, 14200 US-1, Juno Beach, FL 33408
kid: Watch a healed sea turtle crawl back into the ocean while everyone cheers. In summer there are night turtle walks to see nesting mamas.
dad: Follow the center's release announcements and drop everything when one is scheduled. Turtle walks are June–July; book early.
tip: Releases are announced a day or two ahead on the center's channels. Turtle walks have a minimum age; check.
wonder: How does a turtle find its way across the ocean without a map?

name: Rollerblade the Jupiter Riverwalk
addr: Harbourside Place, 200 US-1, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: A smooth, wide path right along the water from Harbourside all the way toward the inlet. Blades, scooters or bikes, with boats and pelicans the whole way.
dad: Park free at Harbourside, blade north to the inlet and back. Ice cream at Harbourside is the finish line.
tip: Free. About 2.5 miles end to end; the inlet section was the last to open, so check how far you can go. Helmets on.
wonder: Why is the water in the Intracoastal calm when the ocean is rough?

name: Jupiter Skate Park at Abacoa
addr: 1501 W Frederick Small Rd, Jupiter, FL 33458
kid: A big concrete bowl for boards and scooters, plus two outdoor roller hockey rinks you can inline skate on when no league is playing.
dad: Bring the blades for the hockey rinks and a board for the bowl edges. Watch the big kids drop in, then try the smallest ramp together.
tip: Free, helmets required, sessions may need a reservation. Call (561) 630-5684 for open-skate hours.
wonder: Why do you go faster coming down the bowl than you went up?

name: ArtiGras Fine Arts Festival
addr: Abacoa Town Center, 1200 Town Center Dr, Jupiter, FL 33458
kid: Hundreds of artists in tents, a youth art competition, and a kids' zone where you make your own art to take home.
dad: Give them a small budget to buy one real piece from a real artist and talk to them about how they made it.
tip: Mid-February, Saturday and Sunday. Kids' tickets are cheap or free; check the site.
wonder: How many tries do you think the artist needed before this one came out right?

name: Jupiter Jubilee
addr: Jupiter Community Center, 200 Military Trail, Jupiter, FL 33458
kid: The town's own free festival: bounce houses, a touch-a-truck line of fire engines and police cars, live music and food trucks.
dad: Climb into the fire truck with them. Find the booth with the town's old photos and spot places you know.
tip: Free. Early February, one Saturday. Arrive early for parking.
wonder: What is the oldest thing in Jupiter? Ask at the history booth.

name: Jupiter Seafood Festival
addr: Carlin Park, 400 S State Rd A1A, Jupiter, FL 33477
kid: A food festival right on the beach with crab, shrimp, music and a kids' area. Eat with sand on your feet.
dad: Try one new sea creature each. Walk the beach after and talk about where it came from.
tip: One weekend in late February at Carlin Park. Bring cash and a blanket.
wonder: Which of these foods was swimming yesterday? Ask the cook.

name: South Florida Fair
addr: 9067 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33411
kid: The biggest fair of the year: a giant Ferris wheel, rides, farm animals, pig races, fried everything and shows all day.
dad: Ride the Ferris wheel at dusk. Visit the agriculture barns first so the animals get their turn before the rides take over.
tip: About 17 days from mid-January. Ride passes are cheaper online. Weekday afternoons have the shortest lines.
wonder: How does the Ferris wheel keep the seats level while the wheel turns?

name: The Gardens GreenMarket
addr: City Hall, 10500 N Military Trail, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
kid: Sunday morning market with fresh fruit, honey, pastries, live music and a kids' corner. Pick what we eat for breakfast.
dad: Give each kid five dollars and one job: find the best thing. Eat it on the lawn.
tip: Free entry. Sundays 8 to 1, October through May, on the City Hall lawn.
wonder: Why can we grow strawberries here in January?

name: TurtleFest at Loggerhead
addr: 14200 US-1, Juno Beach, FL 33408
kid: A two-day sea turtle party: music, games, a kids' zone, food trucks and the turtle hospital open the whole time.
dad: Go on the quieter of the two days. Sign them up for the kids' activities in the morning before the crowd.
tip: Free admission. Dates move between February and March; check the center's site.
wonder: Why do we turn off beach lights during nesting season?

name: Stargazing at the FAU Observatory
addr: FAU Science Building SE-43, 777 Glades Rd, Boca Raton, FL 33431
kid: Look through a real university telescope at Saturn's rings, Jupiter's moons and craters on our Moon. Real astronomers answer your questions.
dad: Pick a night when Saturn or Jupiter is up. Let them ask the astronomer one question each; practice it in the car.
tip: Free, no reservation. Weather permitting; check the FAU page the day of. It's a drive, so make it a late-night special.
wonder: How long did the light from Saturn travel to reach your eye tonight?

name: STEAM Saturday at the Gardens Library
addr: Gardens Branch Library, 11303 Campus Dr, Palm Beach Gardens, FL 33410
kid: Robots, slime, LEGO builds and science experiments at our own library, plus a stack of books to take home.
dad: Pull up the branch calendar together and let them circle the program. Stay after and each pick a book about what you just did.
tip: Free with a library card. Programs are on the PBC Library calendar; the Jupiter branch runs them too.
wonder: What's one question you want answered today? Let's find the book.

name: Shark Tooth Hunting at Juno Beach
addr: Juno Beach Park, 14775 US-1, Juno Beach, FL 33408
kid: Real fossil shark teeth wash up on our beaches, especially after a storm. Learn to spot the shiny black triangles in the shell piles.
dad: Go at low tide after rough surf. Sift the shell line by the pier. A jar of teeth on the shelf keeps the curiosity going.
tip: Free. Best after a storm, on a falling tide. Bring a small sieve or just sharp eyes.
wonder: Why are shark teeth black when the shark's teeth are white?

name: Mounts Botanical Garden
addr: 531 N Military Trail, West Palm Beach, FL 33415
kid: A garden with a walkway over the water, giant lily pads, a butterfly garden and plants that smell like chocolate and lemon.
dad: Do the scavenger hunt from the front desk. Smell, touch and ask a gardener what grows in our own yard.
tip: Kids under a certain age are free; check. Mornings are coolest. Special light shows some winters.
wonder: Why do some flowers only open at night?

name: Feast of Little Italy
addr: Abacoa Town Center, 1200 Town Center Dr, Jupiter, FL 33458
kid: Carnival rides, cannoli, pizza, music and a stretch-the-string-cheese contest, all in one weekend at Abacoa.
dad: Friday evening is calmest. One ride each, one new food each.
tip: Free admission; rides and food cost. Early November, Friday to Sunday.
wonder: How does string cheese get its strings?
